stem.en: The nucleus is often called the "brain" of the cell. Why can this comparison mislead a student?

text.en: The nucleus holds no information at all, because all of it is held in the cell membrane.

feedback.en: The nucleus holds the DNA, so it does hold the information.

text.en: The nucleus releases all the energy of a cell, which is not something that a brain does.

feedback.en: Mitochondria supply the energy needed for most cell activities, not the nucleus.

text.en: Every cell, including every bacterium, has one large nucleus, but not every animal has a brain.

feedback.en: Bacteria have no well-defined nucleus, so this statement is false.

text.en: A nucleus holds instructions, but it does not think.

explanation.en: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell through the information in its DNA. It does not think, plan or decide.

hints.en: What does a brain do that a nucleus does not?
